text: Section 103 BNS 2023 prescribes punishment for murder. Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine. Section 103(2) introduces a specific aggravated penalty where a group of five or more persons acting in concert commits murder on grounds of race, caste, community, sex, place of birth, language, personal belief or any other ground (mob lynching), punishable with death or life imprisonment.

marginal_heading: Cheating and Dishonestly Inducing Delivery of Property (Replaces Section 420 IPC)
text: Section 318 BNS defines and penalizes Cheating. Section 318(4) provides that whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

Section 356 BNS penalizes criminal defamation. Whoever, by words spoken or intended to be read, or by signs or visible representations, makes or publishes any imputation concerning any person intending to harm reputation, is punishable with simple imprisonment up to two years, or with fine, or with both, or with community service.

marginal_heading: Arrest without Warrant & Notice of Appearance (Replaces Section 41 & 41A CrPC)
text: Section 35 BNSS regulates police powers of arrest. For offences punishable with imprisonment up to seven years, arrest cannot be made mechanically. Police officer must serve a Notice of Appearance under Section 35(3) directing the accused to appear. Section 35(7) mandates prior permission from an officer not below Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) before arresting any person who is infirm or aged above sixty years.

marginal_heading: First Information Report (FIR) & e-FIR / Zero FIR (Replaces Section 154 CrPC)
text: Section 173 BNSS mandates compulsory registration of FIR for cognizable offences. Features: (1) Zero FIR: can be registered at ANY police station irrespective of jurisdiction; (2) e-FIR: electronic communication can be submitted, signed within three days; (3) Preliminary Inquiry (PI): permitted only for offences punishable between 3 to 7 years, strictly capped at 14 days.

marginal_heading: Remedies on Police Refusal & Magistrate Directive (Replaces Section 154(3) & 156(3) CrPC)
text: Section 175 BNSS outlines legal remedies when police refuse to register an FIR: (1) Under Section 175(4), representation with postal proof to Superintendent of Police (SP); (2) Under Section 175(3), application before Judicial Magistrate accompanied by an affidavit verifying refusal, upon which Magistrate can order police to register FIR and investigate.

marginal_heading: Regular Bail and Anticipatory Bail (Replaces Section 437, 438, 439 CrPC)
text: Section 480 BNSS governs release on bail in non-bailable offences by Magistrates and Courts. Section 482 BNSS empowers the High Court and Court of Session to grant Anticipatory Bail to any person who has reason to believe that they may be arrested on an accusation of having committed a non-bailable offence, subject to statutory conditions of non-tampering and cooperation.

marginal_heading: Admissibility of Electronic Records & Mandatory Certificate (Replaces Section 65B IEA)
text: Section 61 BSA recognizes electronic and digital records as primary evidence. Section 63 BSA establishes the mandatory certificate for admissibility of electronic records (emails, server logs, WhatsApp chats, CCTV, phone recordings). Certificate must identify the device, certify lawful custody, describe hashing/tamper-proof integrity, and be signed by the custodian or manager of the device.

marginal_heading: Market Value, Multiplier Factor & 100% Solatium Award
text: Mandates determination of market value under Section 26. Section 27 applies a statutory multiplier factor (up to 2.0x) for rural land. Section 30 mandates payment of 100% Solatium (bonus equal to 100% of the market value) over and above the compensation amount, plus 12% per annum additional compensation from the date of preliminary notification to the date of Collector's award.

marginal_heading: Reference to Land Acquisition Authority for Enhanced Compensation
text: Section 64 provides that any interested person who has not accepted the award of the Collector regarding measurement, amount of compensation, or apportionment, may submit a written application to the Collector within six weeks requiring the matter to be referred to the Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority (LARR Authority) for judicial enhancement of compensation.

marginal_heading: Persons not to be deprived of property save by authority of law
text: Article 300A guarantees that no person shall be deprived of their property save by authority of law. The Supreme Court (in Sukh Dutt Ratra, Tukaram Kana Joshi, and Vidarbha Irrigation) held that taking private land for public infrastructure (canals, roads) without lawful acquisition or compensation is an unconstitutional expropriation violating human rights, enabling High Court Writs under Art 226 for compound interest and solatium.

marginal_heading: Power of High Courts to issue certain writs
text: Article 226 empowers High Courts throughout territories in relation to which they exercise jurisdiction to issue directions, orders or writs, including Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo Warranto, and Certiorari, for enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose against State instrumentalities and government departments.

marginal_heading: Dishonour of Cheque for Insufficiency of Funds & Strict 30-Day Limitation
text: Section 138 imposes criminal liability for dishonour of cheques for insufficiency of funds. Statutory prerequisites: (1) Cheque presented within validity; (2) Statutory Legal Demand Notice served within 30 days of bank return memo; (3) 15 days cure window given to drawer. Section 142 prescribes strict limitation: complaint must be instituted within one month (30 days) from the date cause of action arises under clause (c).

marginal_heading: Consent Architecture, Data Fiduciary Obligations & Penalties up to ₹250 Crores
citation: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, Sec. 6 & 33
text: Section 6 DPDP Act mandates that processing of digital personal data requires clear, specific, informed, and unconditional consent with a separate notice. Data Fiduciaries must implement technical and organizational measures to prevent breach. Section 33 and the Schedule prescribe civil penalties: up to ₹250 Crores for failure to prevent data breaches, and up to ₹200 Crores for failure to protect children's data.

marginal_heading: Application for Compensation before Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT)
text: Section 166 governs claim petitions for compensation arising out of motor accidents causing death or bodily injury. Under the 2019/2022 Amendment, an application must be filed within six months of the occurrence of the accident. Claims Tribunal determines just compensation including pecuniary losses (loss of income, medical bills) and non-pecuniary heads (pain and suffering, loss of consortium).

marginal_heading: Devolution of Interest in Coparcenary Property (Equal Rights for Daughters)
text: Section 6 (amended by Act 39 of 2005) provides that a daughter of a coparcener shall by birth become a coparcener in her own right in the same manner as the son, with identical rights and liabilities in coparcenary property. In Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma (2020) 9 SCC 1, a 3-Judge Supreme Court bench confirmed that this right is retroactive and unconditional, irrespective of whether the father was alive on September 9, 2005.

citation: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, Order 39 Rules 1 & 2
text: Order 39 Rules 1 and 2 CPC empower civil courts to grant temporary injunctions restraining defendants from wasting, damaging, alienating, selling, removing or disposing of property, or dispossessing the plaintiff. The applicant must prove three mandatory legal pillars: (1) Strong prima facie case; (2) Balance of convenience in plaintiff's favor; (3) Irreparable injury/loss that cannot be compensated in monetary damages.
